title: That Endless Green
subtitle: One among countless in the world. One that belongs only to your memory.

trails.title: The Sound of Prejudice
trails.description: If you tear down the walls you've built, you may grow.

content.text:
There was once a divide between the two.
It was life. It was death. It was a bout of rain.
Those who came after questionedthe true nature of the divide.
It was bloodline. It was reason. It was a flash of insight.
A brave soul leaps across and turns to look back at the divide.
He sees a door never meant to be openedand an imaginary wall.

items.text: *knock*
All for nothing.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Next time a colleague disappears without a trace, they'd better leave behind more clues first.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Not even a crack. This isn't drawn on, is it?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: No visible locks. No signs of arcane skills, either.
But to whom?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Greta's been here. She found a way through. There must be a way.

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher I
items.text: Researcher Adler?

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher I
items.text: Researcher Adler, how are you? We've all been quite concerned about your condition.

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher I
items.text: The results of our investigation into the "Storm" have arrived, and everyone's fighting to form research teams. This might be a bit presumptuous, but we'd like to invite you to join us.

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher II
items.text: That's right! You probably don't remember, but during a cryptography lecture at the University of Göttingen, you said, "Every puzzle has a solution," and that if there's no answer, it's just because we haven't figured out the rules yet.

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher II
items.text: This is just like that—a crossword puzzle that nobody's ever solved! We'll be entering new territory! The first to research the "Storm"!

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher I
items.text: And we'll be the first to find a solution—to figure out the truth!
He stares at the crossword before him, the letters in its squares drowned in ink so thick they're illegible.
Just like the "Storm," covering everything, with no pattern at all.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: A solution?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: A "solution" that can be overturned at any time by the appearance of an inexplicable presence?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Only a fanatic would find joy in all this. At least they finally have some evidence that gods are real.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I hear they've given you a nickname, dear brother.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Hmm.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: "Enigma." You must admit your colleagues have quite the sense of humor and taste, if you ask me.
She sets down a stack of files.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: You may be helping with some decoding work in here, and somehow turned me into your personal news and paper delivery girl.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: But this house isn't a laboratory, nor your dorm, and it's certainly not an emergency shelter.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: There is no harm in returning to a normal life.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I'm listening.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: No, you aren't.
Enigma sighs and sets down the squash ball in his hand.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Alright, fine. I'll say what you want me to say: How's the situation outside, Greta?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Everyone must be very busy. They've given up on sending smart robots to my door, and they haven't asked me to join their various research teams for quite some time.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Has the "Storm" research had any new breakthroughs? Is everyone in high spirits? Busy coming up with great ideas?
She's quiet for a moment, then shakes her head slightly.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Another "Storm" hit. It was sudden. I heard there were researchers gathering data outside. They didn't make it back in time.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The situation at the Foundation isn't much better.
He wants to slam his fist on the table. Instead, he just pushes the papers aside, exhausted.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Is that so? I see.
There must be a reason. Something that has driven you here, to stand before this door. To demand a response that has never come.
Self-expectations.

items.speaker: Adler
items.text: I've attended lectures at Laplace. Their researchers firmly believe they can discover the truth. It's utter conceit.

items.speaker: Adler
items.text: But that's the way it should be.
Others' expectations.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I'll take up that role and do what you've been nagging me to do. I'll take care of those pesky committees.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: But just so you know, I'm not doing this for the higher-ups who look down on us—

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: But for the people who look up to us from below!
A wish to change everything.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Because I want Laplace to remain a place for people like you.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Someone has to do something.
He has never truly looked at this door. Difficulties and obstacles are common in research. Every result is built on countless failures.
For the first time, he takes a few steps back to get a clear look at this old enemy, the one he has been wrestling with for as long as he can remember.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I should've done this a long time ago. No.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: No need to speculate on how the past could have gone. There's an excellent opportunity—right here and now.
The Picrasma extract is wearing off. His heartbeat pounds in his ears as everything he perceives slowly returns to what it was.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Everything inside the toybox changes with observation. It faithfully recreates my every thought, perception, and idea.
Maybe it's the side effects of the extract. Maybe it's the absurdity of what he sees, and how unsurprising it all is. A searing pain rises behind his eyes.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Hah. Turns out there was no wall around the door after all.
An unknown darkness engulfs him.
He steps forward with ease.
Field, Toybox
The place where his toybox journey began. The place where it ends.
Every journey began at this field. He recognizes the feeling of the grass beneath his boots.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Hm. Back where I started?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Not bad.
Parting the blades, he makes his way toward the center.
The core rests there in the grass, waiting for the next stubborn seeker to pick it up.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: The core can read one's thoughts, and make the toybox manifest whatever one desires most.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: I wanted to create a language without limits, a language everyone could understand and use. And so, it rebuilt the Tower of Babel for me.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: It is far too powerful. If you take it, you'll be engulfed by it—something I don't want to happen.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: But it's clear you've made your decision. I'm powerless to stop you. I can only wish you the best of luck, and hope you stay true to your convictions.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: If I had the time, I'd like to have witnessed what it creates for you.

There is endless green in countless places. Maybe it's the mountaintop he once reached. Maybe it's the graveyard he can't bring himself to visit. Maybe it's the open field in front of the Laplace building.
All he wanted was to return to that first field of grass.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Alright. Adventure's over.
Enigma bends down and picks up the core.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Good. It's created a new code under my observation. A familiar, basic code.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: And, a hint.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: "The age of humans has come to an end."
He reads the words under his breath.
This is as close to reality as the simulation gets—replicating appearance, language, and thought. The data does its job, producing the most reasonable result it can.
In the real world, there is a note just like this in his drawer, taken from that pioneer's journal. She found the answer. Even here, in the simulation.
Proof that she will walk this path every time, without exception. A prophecy written in data.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Ha. Arcanum.
